newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish state to evaluate Tele Danmark.
newsitem.headline: Danish state to evaluate Tele Danmark.

text.p: The Danish government is setting up a working group to assess the value of its 51 percent holding in telecoms group Tele Danmark A/S but it denied that the move was a direct prelude to further privatisation.
"A sale is not imminent, but when it is taken up at the political level one will have to decide what is the best course of action," research ministry official Knud Larsen told Reuters.
The market is betting on a selloff in 1998.
The government has said that it does not intend to retain its holding permanently but that there will be no sale this year.

Since its partial privatisation in 1994 Tele Danmark, with current market capitalisation of around $3.1 billion, has gone into several foreign ventures, bought up local cable television providers and producers and expanded in many directions.

"The resources that the state has in Tele Danmark are so great that it would be irresponsible not to get the best possible advice on how best to take care of its assets. What the conclusion will be, has absolutely not been decided yet," Larsen said.
Telecoms analysts point to the June 1998 completion date for the rationalisation of Tele Danmark's equity structure.
They say that this, and Wednesday's announcement of staff cuts and organisational changes to be carried out within the same period, indicate a likely sale in 1998, an election year.
The new working group is expected to report on the company's worth late in 1997.
